newsitem.title: USA: Archer plan would restructure U.S. air ticket tax.
newsitem.headline: Archer plan would restructure U.S. air ticket tax.

text.p: U.S. House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer on Monday proposed restructuring domestic air travel taxes and boosting fees on international travel.
The plan would cut the domestic ticket tax to 7.5 percent from 10 percent currently, but impose a $2 per-person, per-leg, charge on those same flights.
The Texas Republican would also raise international departure fees to $10 per passenger from $6 now and charge arriving passengers $10.
The changes would shift the cost of aviation infrastructure maintenance towards those who use it most without reducing current federal revenues, Archer said.
"The revenue that is raised out of what is now the ticket tax will continue to be roughly the same, although the formula for implementation is different," Archer told reporters.
"Some people are paying a lot less as their prorata share than others. We haven't totally solved the equity problem, but we have moved in the direction of solving that problem," he added.
Archer said U.S. international flight fees were among the lowest in the world and his plan would move to correct that.
"There are very, very few (countries) that have a lower exit fee and we're raising that to $10, which is still lower than the majority of the other countries in the world," Archer said.
The two-dollar domestic ticket fee would gradually rise to $3 dollars in 2002, and subsequently would be indexed for inflation using the consumer price index, according to the plan.
Similarly, the $10 international fee would be indexed using the CPI beginning on January 1, 1999.
